provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation:
In the original puzzle, bars stand on the bottom row and fall to the right. The factory works out where that picture ends up after the D4 transform. It maps two direction vectors through the transform: canonical 'up' (-1,0) and canonical 'right' (0,1). Mirroring negates dc, and each clockwise turn sends (dr,dc) to (dc,-dr). The edge opposite the transformed 'up' is the base the bars stand on (bottom, top, left or right). The transformed 'right' gives the fall direction along that edge (STEP = +1 or -1). Colour roles become constants: BG = palette[0], pusher = palette[1], follower = palette[2].

The emitted program works directly in the visible grid:
1. Every line perpendicular to the base that holds non-background cells is one bar. The generator never puts bars in neighbouring lines, so each such line is exactly one bar. Its height is its count of non-background cells.
2. Bars are processed in fall order along the base.
3. A pusher-coloured bar always falls. Any other bar falls only if the previous bar fell and this bar sits at or before the cell just past the previous tip, i.e. (i - (prev_i + STEP*prev_h))*STEP <= 0.
4. A falling bar's cells become background. Its colour is then painted along the base line from its own position for its height in the STEP direction, clipped to the grid.

This matches the constructor's rule (knock iff the previous bar fell and last == col) and the archived solver's x <= prev_end + 1 test. All three train and both test fixtures follow this uniform rule; there were no contradictions.
draft_notes.limitations:
Not tested here; the host will run the verification.

- Background, pusher and follower colours are taken from palette[0], palette[1] and palette[2], not inferred from the demonstrations.
- Each line perpendicular to the base is assumed to hold at most one bar, grounded on the base. This holds in the generator because bar positions are always at least 2 apart.
- Any non-pusher colour can be knocked over, as in the archived solver; the domain only has the follower colour.
- The fall is clipped at the grid edge, though the generator never needs this.
- No constructor defects or hidden tie-breaks were found.
